_partNote: Class images for the explorer tiles, rendered at about 74px. Three of the seven are antennas, so they are deliberately given opposite shapes: a flared rectangular horn, a tall pole with a triangular crown of flat panels, and a plain sphere on a pedestal. The sphere also keeps this sheet's satellite tile away from the dish and the flat panel already used on the space-launch sheet. Class IV uses a submarine repeater rather than a cable reel, since a reel is already the grid sheet's class II. Class VII is an abstraction, so it takes a plain padlock, the same way the space sheet draws a schematic globe for its orbits class. The style override has to forbid yellow and orange by name: fiber jackets, patch cords and warning labels are all that color in life.
style: Minimalist technical illustration, the style of a precise patent drawing crossed with an isometric product sketch. Uniform-weight dark slate-gray ink linework with sparse, muted steel-blue accent shading (hex 4E7AA8) on a plain very light warm-gray background (hex F2F3F1). Three-quarter isometric view, single centered subject, generous margins. No text, no labels, no callouts, no logos, no humans, no background scenery, no drop shadows. Clean, engineered, calm. Strictly two colors plus the background: dark slate-gray line and muted steel-blue fill. Every material, including optical fiber, cable jackets, patch cords, connectors and circuit board substrate, is drawn in that same palette. Absolutely no copper, brass, bronze, gold, orange, red, yellow or green anywhere, even where the real object would be that color. No indicator lights, no glowing elements, no radio waves, no signal arcs and no beams of any kind. Favor open, airy linework with large unfilled light areas over heavy solid gray shading; the drawing should read as line art, not as a rendered solid model. Draw the subject as one whole object seen from outside. Do not draw a cutaway, a section view or an exploded assembly.

partPrompts.1: A single rectangular horn antenna standing on a small plain stand, seen three-quarter: a straight square-section tube at the back that flares outward in four flat straight-sided panels to a large open rectangular mouth at the front, with a plain square bolted flange where the tube meets the stand. The open mouth is the widest part and reads as a clean rectangular opening. One object, pointing slightly across the frame. No dish, no curve, no reflector, no cables, no mast.
partPrompts.2: A single cellular monopole tower standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a tall plain tapering tube, very tall and thin, carrying a triangular platform frame near the top with one flat rectangular panel antenna mounted vertically on each of its three sides, and a small drum-shaped microwave antenna clamped to the tube a short way below. Tall and slender, the triangular crown of flat panels the identifying feature. No lattice bracing, no guy wires, no conductors, no buildings, no ground detail.
partPrompts.3: A satellite earth station radome on a pedestal, seen three-quarter: one large smooth sphere sitting on a short cylindrical base, the sphere marked only by a few faint great-circle seam lines where its panels meet, standing on a low square plinth. Simple and geometric, the sphere dominant and the base clearly secondary. No dish inside, no antenna, no window, no opening, no flat panels, no lattice, no building.
partPrompts.4: A submarine cable repeater lying horizontally on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a long slender cylindrical pressure housing with smoothly tapered ends, several plain raised bands running around it at intervals, and one heavy cable leaving the center of each tapered end and running straight out of frame in opposite directions. Long, smooth and symmetrical, clearly much longer than it is thick. No reel, no drum, no coiled cable, no ship, no water, no connectors.
partPrompts.5: A free-space optical terminal on a two-axis gimbal, seen three-quarter: a short stout barrel with one plain flat circular window at its front face, held between the two arms of a U-shaped yoke by pivots on each side, the yoke standing on a squat cylindrical turntable base. Compact and mechanical, the U-yoke the identifying geometry. Not a camera and not a telescope on a tripod: no lens rings, no viewfinder, no three legs, no beam, no light coming out of the window.
partPrompts.6: A single rack-mount equipment chassis lying flat, seen three-quarter: a wide thin rectangular metal box, much wider than it is deep and very shallow in height, with a flat mounting ear standing out at each end of the front face, a row of eight identical small square ports along the lower half of that face, and a plain vented strip along the upper half. Flat, wide and blank, one unit alone. No rack frame, no cables, no other units stacked above or below, no display, no indicator lights.
partPrompts.7: A single closed padlock standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a chunky rounded-rectangular body with softly radiused corners and a thick U-shaped shackle rising from its top face, both ends of the shackle seated in the body, and one plain round keyway recessed in the front face. Solid and geometric, the U over a block the whole silhouette. One padlock alone: no key, no chain, no hasp, no door, no markings.
